proof.criterion: The listener notices a dead hub in seconds (roll call 3, the spec's own acceptance): a test stops answering the listener's pings without closing its socket, and the listener reports the connection lost within 5 seconds; the test fails at the base.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary, started as production starts it, against an in-process NATS whose relay stops moving bytes in both directions with both sides' connections kept (testnats.Server.Freeze).
proof.command: From packages/envoy: `go test -count=3 -timeout 10m -run 'TestBothOfTheListenersNATSClientsReportASilentCutWithinSeconds$' ./cmd/listener/` at the head; the same test file over a clean copy of the base's cmd/listener/main.go and live_topics.go at base e4c9ab85.
proof.observed: Head: 3 of 3 runs passed, each client's `envoy nats disconnected` line 2.79 to 2.85 s after the freeze, for both client names (`envoy` and `envoy-live-topics`), which is what pins both call sites. Base: FAIL after 7.032 s, `no disconnect line for envoy and envoy-live-topics 5.021s into a silent cut`.
proof.negativeControl: The base run above is the control for the change, and the test's own shape is the control for the test: it goes through listenerStreamOptions and openLiveTopics rather than passing bus.WithSilentCutDetection itself, so a copy of the existing bus-level test would have passed at the base and proven nothing. A run with the option removed from both call sites fails the same way as the base.

proof.surface: The daemon's own natsauth.Connect, called as internal/daemon/workflow.go calls it (LogEvents and ReconnectForever), against a server that answers the handshake PING and then answers nothing with the socket open.
proof.command: From packages/daemon: `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=2 -timeout 10m -run 'TestAHubThatStopsAnsweringIsNoticedWithinSeconds$' ./internal/natsauth/` at the head; the same test file over the base's natsauth.go at base e4c9ab85.
proof.observed: Head: 2 of 2 passed under -race, the cut noticed 3.01 s after the server went quiet, with `NATS connection lost` in the captured log and IsConnected false. Base: FAIL after 5.030 s, `the connection was not reported lost within 5.014592798s of the server going quiet: IsConnected = true, the warning logged = false`.
proof.negativeControl: The base run. The pings are set inside Connect rather than by its caller, so the test covers the production path: a caller-passed option would have left workflow.go's one call untested.

proof.criterion: Item 1.8: startDispatchStream waits for this client's own reconcile, so a check that the next start wrote nothing cannot pass before that start wrote anything.
proof.surface: The dispatch start on one in-process NATS server, through the helper production's own test uses, and the bus client's new accessor.
proof.command: From packages/envoy: `go test -count=5 -timeout 10m -run 'TestADefaultDispatchStartOnASingleServerCreatesEverythingAtOneCopyAndTheNextWritesNothing$' ./cmd/dispatch/` and the same under `CGO_ENABLED=1 … -race`; `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestHookedConnectionEventsCountsTheFirstReconcileOfABackgroundClient$' ./internal/bus/`.
proof.observed: All green at the head. The accessor's meaning was proven before the helper used it: 0 hooked connection events before a background owning client's first connection, at least 1 once its first reconcile had run, after which the stream reads back.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 6: the Go suites of packages/envoy, the claude-envoy tests and the dist-freshness check, and (the plan's addition) the envoy-client stall suites and the packages/daemon suite, pass at the head.

proof.criterion: Roll call 5, the architect's decision of 2026-10-30: a watch a rewatch replaced ends without an ERROR line, and a watch that fails while it is still the live one keeps its ERROR.
proof.surface: The kvwatch package's own watcher against a real in-process NATS server, both branches driven directly; and the real envoy-listener binary with its three caches, against a hub whose relay freezes and thaws.
proof.command: From packages/envoy: `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=2 -timeout 15m -run 'TestAFailedFirstStartLogsItsErrorOnlyWhileItIsTheLiveWatch$' ./internal/kvwatch/`; `go test -count=1 -timeout 15m -run 'TestASilentCutRewatchesTheCachesWithNoErrorLine$' ./cmd/listener/`; `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/kvwatch/ ./internal/cistore/ ./internal/session/ ./internal/store/`.
proof.observed: Both rows of the unit test pass twice under -race: a first watch that fails with no replacement current logs the one ERROR; one that fails after a Rewatch armed a replacement logs no ERROR of any message, one INFO end line, and its replacement still delivers a later put. The listener guard is green: both clients' cut lines, a warm-up line from each of the three caches after the thaw, an interest from another listener reaching this one's cache, and no ERROR line from the freeze on. kvwatch and its three dependants are green under -race (65.021s, 22.111s, 11.620s, 32.918s).
proof.negativeControl: With Start's old body restored and the test files untouched, the unit test's `a rewatch replaced it` row fails: `a first watch a rewatch replaced logged [test cache watch failed: nats: connection closed], want no ERROR`. The listener guard does not go red there, and no listener-process test can: main.go opens all three caches and waits out their warm-up gates before it adds the reconnect hook, so no first watch is in flight when a Rewatch can exist (a probe froze the hub for 4.8 s and for 40 s and reached that branch neither time). The unit test is the red-at-base proof; the listener test is the end-to-end guard, and its doc comment says so.

The two ERROR lines the tester recorded (`interest registry watch failed`, `role claims watch failed`, `nats: connection closed`) do not come from the listener binary: they come from the test process's own second registry (store.Open(writer), the other-listener helper of cmd/listener/restart_test.go:31-49), whose connection the test closes while its first watches are still in flight. Those watchers are the live ones, so they keep their ERROR, which the architect's decision asks for.

testerFailureAnswered.failure: The head carried no CI at all: round 1's push ended on the implement handoff commit, which carried `skip-checks: true`, so GitHub started no run for a push that also carried seven code commits. The reviewer reads the head's checks and a base that requires a check will not merge a head whose checks never ran.
testerFailureAnswered.fix: This round's push ends on a commit with no such line, so GitHub runs the base's required checks over every code commit of this branch. The rule the round broke is that a round whose code and handoff go in one push is a code push; this round's handoff commit carries no trailer.
testerFailureAnswered.notRewritten: The two trailered commits already on the branch are left as they are. Rewriting mine alone would leave the tester's own handoff commit as the tip, which carries the line correctly (its push was handoff-only) and would still start no run; rewriting both would rewrite the commit the daemon recorded as the tester's handoff. What starts CI is the push, not the history. Reported to the architect, whose instruction named the rewrite.
